source:
# JSON (RFC 8259): the data-interchange grammar — the fleet's first
# general-purpose data format flavor, and the shared corpus grammar for
# the industry benchmark suite (parsanol-rs#526: every competitor engine
# has a JSON grammar, so the comparison row is direct).
#
# Edition-2 notes: the object/array recursions are right-recursive
# through their element lists (no left recursion). Whitespace is RFC ws
# (space/tab/LF/CR), zero-or-more, handled positionally around the
# structural tokens. The true/false/null faces are exact: the value
# grammar's ordered choice plus the document-end anchor make "truex" a
# reject without a trailing guard.

grammar Json version "1.0.0" edition 2 {
  ws = *( %x20 / %x09 / %x0A / %x0D )

  ## A JSON text is a serialized value (RFC 8259 section 2: "a JSON
  ## text is a serialized value"); parsers accept the value with
  ## optional surrounding whitespace.
  json = ws value ws

  value = object / array / string / number / %i"true" / %i"false" / %i"null"

  object = ( "{" ws [ member *( ws "," ws member ) ] ws "}" ) as object
  member = ( string ws ":" ws value ) as member

  array = ( "[" ws [ value *( ws "," ws value ) ] ws "]" ) as array

  ## Strings (RFC 8259 section 7): the unescaped class excludes quote
  ## and backslash; the escape set is the nine two-char forms including
  ## the u-hexquad.
  string = ( %x22 *( %x20-21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-10FFFF / %x5C ( %x22 / %x5C / %x2F / %x62 / %x66 / %x6E / %x72 / %x74 / ( %x75 4*( %x30-39 / %x41-46 / %x61-66 ) ) ) ) %x22 ) as string

  ## Numbers (RFC 8259 section 6): minus optional, int is zero or a
  ## nonzero-leading digit run, frac and exp optional.
  number = ( [ %x2D ] int [ frac ] [ exp ] ) as number
  int = %x30 / ( %x31-39 *digit )
  frac = %x2E 1*digit
  exp = ( %x65 / %x45 ) [ %x2B / %x2D ] 1*digit
  digit = %x30-39

  entry main: json

  test {
    accept "{}"
    accept "[]"
    accept "{\"a\": 1}"
    accept "{\"a\": [1, true, null], \"b\": \"x\\nA\"}"
    accept "[[[[[1]]]]]"
    accept "-0.5e10"
    accept "\"a\\tb\\\\c\\/d\""
    accept "\"A plain hex\""
    accept "{ \"nested\" : { \"deep\" : [ {\"x\" : 0} ] } }"
    reject "{a: 1}"
    reject "{'a': 1}"
    reject "[1, 2,]"
    reject "truex"
    reject "01"
    reject "+1"
    reject "{\"a\": }"
    reject "\"unterminated"
    reject "{"
  }
}
